requirements.implementation_scope: Actual finite structural role graph worklist and full supplied raw-axiom closure. Exact byte identity/orientation, duplicates, cycles and first forbidden required occurrence are covered. The raw collector is proved to supply every reached node; missing-node outcomes are impossible at the raw entry points. Only the simple-role restriction is decided. Imported closure assembly, chain regularity, datatype/anonymous/global restrictions and full DL validation remain separate.

requirements.requirement: RoleHierarchyRegularity
requirements.implementation_scope: Full raw-axiom property-hierarchy regularity condition from the 2012 Structural Specification §11.2. Original byte IRI identity and orientation; all ordered chains; top-property exemption, exact two-role transitivity, endpoint recursion, global transitivity and the literal inverse-source condition; inverse-source closure applies to direct targets, without assumed inverse-target invariance. The full finite worklist terminates without fuel. Raw node completeness excludes missing outcomes. Successful concrete relation is a strict order compatible with reverse hierarchy reachability; a rejected forced pair is contained in every permitted ordering. Canonical import assembly and all other DL restrictions remain separate.

requirements.requirement: DatatypeDefinitionAcyclicity
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual supplied complete raw axiom closure and exact IRI byte identity. The proved range collector derives every typed datatype dependency from all six range forms, including literal datatypes in enumerations/facet values; enclosing axiom annotations and untyped facet IRIs add no dependency. Directed reflexive reachability restores its owned input and is total even on repeated/cyclic finite graphs. Incremental checking accepts iff a strict partial order exists on the actual datatype carrier and includes every required smaller-to-defined pair. A rejected original dependency has a reverse path and proves no such order can exist. Nonempty transitive reachability constructs the mathematical order witness. No heuristic fuel or caller node metadata is assumed; this correctness-first graph search may take exponential time. Definition availability/uniqueness is separately proved and composed below; custom datatype literal/restriction positions, normative lexical/facet/value spaces, canonical imports, physical resources and complete DL validation remain separate obligations.

requirements.implementation_scope: Complete standard unary raw OWL language: all 18 class forms, six data ranges and 37 annotated axiom variants. Unordered minimum-two associations count recursive structural equivalence classes, including cardinality omission defaults; required nonempty associations, ordered chain minimum written arity, unary data quantifiers and natural numbers follow from raw types. The explicitly accepted 2014 duplicate-disjointness compatibility rule requires pairwise different original members for DisjointClasses, DisjointUnion member classes, disjoint object/data properties and DifferentIndividuals; this is not an amendment to the 2012 Recommendation. Ordinary association repetitions are retained when two distinct members remain; ordered property chains may repeat. The full recursive closure operation composes these rules with the proved nonempty-key check, is total, accepts iff the independent conjunction holds and preserves the first original annotated failure. Input bytes, lexical/facet/value validity, canonical output, RDF self-disjointness mapping, import scoping and complete DL/reasoning validation remain separate.

requirements.requirement: Functional Syntax complete quoted payload component: escape_total_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual Functional Syntax quoted-string payload reading is now proved total and accepts exactly the independent delimited raw-XML/two-escape byte grammar within the decoded-output byte budget. Opening/closing punctuation, raw multiline Unicode, escaped quote/backslash, canonical encoded-unit concatenation, strict source progress and first original-unit diagnostics are composed without trusting lexer metadata. Every malformed UTF-8, missing unit, wrong raw XML character, foreign escape and budget failure has a grammar/phase-specific specification. Both directions connect the decoded-token grammar with the independently verified complete quoted-string terminal language; every matching source candidate has a payload and a fitting budget guarantees the actual exact payload/end result. The reader stops at the closing quote and does not validate a later source suffix; whole-suffix validation is provided by the separate terminal selector. The separately proved stream lexer composes separators/trivia. Other payload kinds, document parsing/import scopes and OWL decisions remain pending. Physical allocation/stack and cancellation remain separate M8 obligations.

requirements.requirement: Verified ALC concept satisfiability without a TBox: toList_fromList
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ALC concept-satisfiability procedure in the kernel, without a TBox: it decides whether some interpretation has an element in a negation-normal-form concept. Conjunctions are expanded, disjunctions branch, top is dropped and bottom rejects; once only named-class literals and restrictions remain, a named class occurring both positively and negated is a clash, and every existential restriction is decided recursively together with the universal restrictions on the same property, with properties and classes compared by exact IRI spelling. The procedure is proved total by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic pair of the total and the pending concept size. It is proved sound: every acceptance yields an explicit tree interpretation over paths whose root satisfies the concept, built from the successor models of the existential restrictions. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe with an element in the concept forces acceptance. Composed with the proved negation-normal-form translation, the tableau never rejects an OWL class expression with an instance in an OWL interpretation, so every rejection proves the expression empty in every OWL interpretation, which justifies unsatisfiability and subsumption answers for the ALC fragment. This is an internal fragment experiment toward M6: TBox axioms and blocking, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, the OWL-level tree model fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing, ontology-level query reductions and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

The procedure is proved total by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic pair of the total and the pending concept size. It is proved sound: every acceptance yields an explicit tree interpretation over paths whose root satisfies the concept, built from the successor models of the existential restrictions. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe with an element in the concept forces acceptance. Composed with the proved negation-normal-form translation, the tableau never rejects an OWL class expression with an instance in an OWL interpretation, so every rejection proves the expression empty in every OWL interpretation, which justifies unsatisfiability and subsumption answers for the ALC fragment. This is an internal fragment experiment toward M6: TBox axioms and blocking, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, the OWL-level tree model fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing, ontology-level query reductions and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified SH concept satisfiability with respect to a TBox and role axioms, with blocking: sat_mono
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual SH concept-satisfiability procedure with respect to a TBox and role axioms in the kernel: tbox::satisfiable_with decides whether some interpretation in which a negation-normal-form TBox concept holds at every element and the object properties respect a role box (inclusions between named object properties, closed under composition, and transitive named object properties) has an element in a negation-normal-form concept; satisfiable_items does the same for a list of items. It runs the tableau with subset blocking on item lists, where a Through item stands for the universal restriction of a transitive property on a filler of the input. A successor along a property s receives the filler of every universal restriction on a property r with s below r and, for every transitive t with s below t and t below r, the restriction of t on that filler; inclusion is tested by the proved role_box::below. It is proved total by well-founded recursion on the remaining room 2^|closure| - |ancestors|, the total item size and the pending item size, where the finite closure adds to the subconcepts the universal restriction of every transitive property on every universal filler. It is proved sound through Hintikka families whose existential witnesses satisfy everything the universal restrictions require along the role (roleFillers): the interpretation whose elements are the sets of the family, relating two sets along a property when the second satisfies everything the first requires along it, is a model of the TBox concept with an instance of the input, and, when the listed inclusions include their compositions, it respects every listed inclusion and transitivity. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe that respects the role box, satisfies the TBox concept everywhere and has an instance of the input forces acceptance. The ALC entry points satisfiable_in and satisfiable_all run the same procedure with no role axioms and keep their proved ALC statements. The ontology queries read their role box from role axioms (alc_ontology::role_box); inverse roles, number restrictions, nominals, property chains, datatypes and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified ALC concept satisfiability with respect to a TBox, with blocking: satisfiable_in_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ALC concept-satisfiability procedure with respect to a TBox in the kernel: it decides whether some interpretation in which a negation-normal-form TBox concept holds at every element has an element in a negation-normal-form concept (general concept inclusions C ⊑ D can be supplied as the negation normal form of the conjunction of the unions of the complement of C with D). It runs the rules of the plain tableau, adds the TBox concept at the root and at every successor, and blocks, and accepts, a node whose literal set is contained in the literal set of an ancestor on its branch; concepts are compared structurally by exact IRI spelling. It is proved total by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic triple of the remaining room 2^|closure| - |ancestors|, the total concept size and the pending concept size: every unblocked node adds a literal set from the finite subconcept closure of the input and TBox concepts that differs from all of its ancestors' sets, which bounds every branch. It is proved sound through a Hintikka-family certificate: every acceptance yields a finite family of clash-free literal sets that each satisfy the TBox concept, with every existential restriction witnessed inside the family together with the universal restrictions on its property, and the interpretation whose elements are those sets is a model of the TBox concept with an instance of the input concept. It is proved complete: any interpretation in any universe in which the TBox concept holds everywhere and the input concept has an instance forces acceptance. Composed with the proved negation-normal-form translation, the procedure never rejects an OWL class expression with an instance in an OWL interpretation in which the TBox class expression holds at every element, so every rejection proves the expression empty in all such interpretations. This is an internal fragment experiment toward M6; the ontology-level queries and role axioms built on it are separate entries, and the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified ontology-level ALC consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking: all_equal_iff
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ontology-level reasoning in the kernel for ALC with assertions about individuals and role axioms (SH): consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking with respect to an axiom closure. Every supported class axiom is internalized into a negation-normal-form concept that holds at every element exactly when the axiom holds: SubClassOf(C D) becomes the union of the complement of C with D, EquivalentClasses holds all members together or none, DisjointClasses excludes every two member occurrences, DisjointUnion also equates the class with the union of its members, ObjectPropertyDomain and ObjectPropertyRange on a named object property restrict its sources or targets, and declarations, annotation axioms, assertions and role axioms impose nothing; the closure's TBox concept is their conjunction, proved to hold at every element exactly when an interpretation fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing satisfies every axiom that is neither an assertion nor a role axiom. SubObjectPropertyOf with a single named sub-property and a named super-property, EquivalentObjectProperties of named properties and TransitiveObjectProperty of a named property form a role box whose inclusions are closed under composition (each new inclusion adds every inclusion it composes with), proved to be respected by an interpretation exactly when it satisfies these role axioms. Every individual that an assertion mentions gets a node, interned by exact structural equality, and node 0 stands for one further element. ClassAssertion becomes the translated concept at its individual's node, ObjectPropertyAssertion an edge along its named property (an inverse property reverses it), and a NegativeObjectPropertyAssertion contradicts the closure exactly when the same edge is asserted; together with role axioms a negative assertion has no answer yet. The queries add their concepts at node 0 or at the queried individual's node and decide with the verified completion for named individuals under that role box. They answer exactly when the internalization, the role box and all translations succeed, no translated concept uses a built-in object property as a role or a built-in class as an ordinary named class, no assertion or role axiom uses a built-in object property, no negative property assertion occurs together with role axioms, and there is room for the nodes, placed concepts and role box. Each answer is proved to equal the independent Direct Semantics definitions of Consistent, ClassSatisfiable, Subsumed and InstanceOf for any valid vocabulary: every acceptance is turned into an actual OWL model of the closure, built from the completion's model with every individual at its node and every other object property read as there, so that the role axioms hold, the built-in classes and object and data properties fixed and data values, datatypes, literals and facets taken from the datatype map, and every OWL model, in any universe and with any reinterpretation of its anonymous individuals, forces acceptance. SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals, data assertions, negative property assertions together with role axioms, inverse properties and property chains in role axioms, disjoint and inverse property axioms, the other property characteristics, the other axiom forms, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, query answering and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified reasoning with named individuals under role axioms (SH): nodeFillers_mem
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual reasoning with named individuals under role axioms (SH) in the kernel: abox_satisfiable_with decides whether some interpretation in which a negation-normal-form TBox concept holds at every element and the object properties respect a role box (inclusions between named object properties, closed under composition, and transitive named object properties) has an element for every node below a positive count that satisfies the given facts (concepts at nodes, or Through facts standing for universal restrictions on transitive properties) and edges (named object properties between nodes). The completion adds the TBox concept at every node, then adds each fact once: it expands conjunctions, branches on disjunctions and pushes every universal restriction along each edge whose property it includes, giving the target the filler and the restriction on every transitive property in between. Once no fact is pending it checks every node for a clash and decides every existential restriction with the SH TBox tableau, together with what the universal restrictions at the same node require along its role. Termination is proved from the measure (node-closure pairs not yet added, pending facts) over a closure extended with the transitive restrictions. Every acceptance under a closed role box yields an explicit model of the role axioms: one element per node and a disjoint copy of a successor model for every existential obligation, related by single steps along included properties and by paths along transitive ones; it relates node elements exactly as the edges and role axioms entail (an edge along an included property, or a path of such edges along a transitive property). Every model of the role axioms in any universe forces acceptance. The ALC entry point abox_satisfiable is the procedure without role axioms and keeps its proved statement. The ontology queries run it with the role box read from their role axioms; equality between individuals, inverse roles, number restrictions and nominals remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified role boxes from the role axioms of an ontology: copy_property_identity
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual ontology-level reasoning in the kernel for ALC with assertions about individuals and role axioms (SH): consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking with respect to an axiom closure. Every supported class axiom is internalized into a negation-normal-form concept that holds at every element exactly when the axiom holds: SubClassOf(C D) becomes the union of the complement of C with D, EquivalentClasses holds all members together or none, DisjointClasses excludes every two member occurrences, DisjointUnion also equates the class with the union of its members, ObjectPropertyDomain and ObjectPropertyRange on a named object property restrict its sources or targets, and declarations, annotation axioms, assertions and role axioms impose nothing; the closure's TBox concept is their conjunction, proved to hold at every element exactly when an interpretation fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing satisfies every axiom that is neither an assertion nor a role axiom. SubObjectPropertyOf with a single named sub-property and a named super-property, EquivalentObjectProperties of named properties and TransitiveObjectProperty of a named property form a role box whose inclusions are closed under composition (each new inclusion adds every inclusion it composes with), proved to be respected by an interpretation exactly when it satisfies these role axioms. Every individual that an assertion mentions gets a node, interned by exact structural equality, and node 0 stands for one further element. ClassAssertion becomes the translated concept at its individual's node, ObjectPropertyAssertion an edge along its named property (an inverse property reverses it), and a NegativeObjectPropertyAssertion contradicts the closure exactly when the same edge is asserted; together with role axioms a negative assertion has no answer yet. The queries add their concepts at node 0 or at the queried individual's node and decide with the verified completion for named individuals under that role box. They answer exactly when the internalization, the role box and all translations succeed, no translated concept uses a built-in object property as a role or a built-in class as an ordinary named class, no assertion or role axiom uses a built-in object property, no negative property assertion occurs together with role axioms, and there is room for the nodes, placed concepts and role box. Each answer is proved to equal the independent Direct Semantics definitions of Consistent, ClassSatisfiable, Subsumed and InstanceOf for any valid vocabulary: every acceptance is turned into an actual OWL model of the closure, built from the completion's model with every individual at its node and every other object property read as there, so that the role axioms hold, the built-in classes and object and data properties fixed and data values, datatypes, literals and facets taken from the datatype map, and every OWL model, in any universe and with any reinterpretation of its anonymous individuals, forces acceptance. SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals, data assertions, negative property assertions together with role axioms, inverse properties and property chains in role axioms, disjoint and inverse property axioms, the other property characteristics, the other axiom forms, the remaining SROIQ constructors, datatypes, query answering and performance remain pending. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified ALCI concepts with inverse roles: inv_inv

requirements.implementation_scope: Actual cardinality restrictions in the concepts of the completion graph tableau: concepts::Concept has at-least and at-most restrictions on object property expressions, read with the independent OWL definitions AtLeast (an injection of n elements) and AtMost. concepts::translate now covers ALCIQ: ObjectMinCardinality, ObjectMaxCardinality and ObjectExactCardinality, qualified or not, with cardinalities below usize::MAX; it is proved total, returns no result exactly outside ALCIQ (InAlciq, since extended to nominals as Translatable), and keeps the meaning of the expression (or its complement) in every interpretation fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing: the complement of a minimum n is a maximum n-1 (nothing for n = 0), of a maximum n a minimum n+1, and of an exact cardinality their union. concepts::negate builds the complement of a concept in negation normal form and is proved to mean exactly its negation in every interpretation; concepts::copy_concept is proved to copy exactly. requirements.requirement: Verified rule search of the completion graph tableau: contains_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual rule search of the completion graph tableau for SHI with named individuals, proved exact against independent predicates on its lists. A label is a list of indices of literal entries of the concept table; Holds reads conjunctions and disjunctions propositionally and every other entry as membership, and holds is proved to decide it. The searches are proved to return, in a fixed order, a node and an entry it needs and lacks (a requirement at the node, the TBox concept, the concept of a lazy unfolding A ⊑ C whose class the label lists, or what a universal restriction at the other end of a link or tree edge requires along the edge's role in either direction, including the restriction on every transitive role in between), else an unblocked node with an existential restriction without a witness (a child created along an included role, the parent along the inverse of the creating role, or a linked named node, satisfying the filler), else Done exactly when no rule applies (Complete). Blocking is equality blocking: a tree node is blocked when two tree nodes on its path to its named root have the same label, and blocked is proved to decide it. Clashes between a named class or a nominal and its complement are detected by an exact search. The tableau's termination, soundness and completeness are proved separately (Rowl.Completion). No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified model of a complete completion graph: holds_same
requirements.implementation_scope: Model of a complete, clash-free completion graph of the SHI tableau, proved against the direct semantics independently of how the graph was built. Its elements are the named nodes and the labels of the unblocked tree nodes; a named class holds where the label lists it; two named nodes are related along a role when a link's role, or its inverse for the reverse direction, is included in it, and every other pair when each label satisfies what the other requires along the role and its inverse; a role also relates every path of such steps along a transitive role included in it. The truth lemma shows every element satisfies every entry its label holds, and model_of_complete gives a model of the role hierarchy (inclusions, inverses and transitivity) in which the TBox concept and every unfolding hold everywhere and every requirement, link and named label holds, with named nodes related only along links when there are no role axioms and different named nodes as different elements.

requirements.requirement: Verified completion graph tableau: copy_label_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual completion graph tableau for SHI with named individuals (completion::satisfiable), with dependency-directed backjumping, proved total, sound and complete. run terminates on every graph of the right shape: each rule application adds a literal to a label or creates a tree node for an unwitnessed existential restriction, and both decrease a measure that weights every node by the room left below it, which equality blocking bounds through a pigeonhole argument on labels along a tree path. Every node records the branch points its label depends on: a rule adds to a node with the points of the node and its neighbours (rule_deps), a new tree node starts with its parent's points, and a clash reports the points of its node and of the clashing entry. Disjunctions branch on copies of the graph under a fresh branch point; when the left disjunct fails with a clash set without that point, the right disjunct is skipped, otherwise it is tried with the points the failure depended on. A rejection with clash set D is proved to rule out every model, in any universes, that satisfies the label of every node whose points lie in D (FullModel). Clashes are detected on insertion; definitions A ⊑ C are unfolded lazily. satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions, closes the table under the restrictions of transitive roles and runs the tableau from one blank named node per individual. An acceptance is proved to come with a model (in Type) of the role hierarchy in which the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at its named nodes, with named nodes related only along links when there are no role axioms and different named nodes as different elements; a rejection is proved to rule out every such model in any universes. A nominal or a cardinality restriction that reaches a label gives no answer, and otherwise None reports only a usize capacity limit.

Disjunctions branch on copies of the graph under a fresh branch point; when the left disjunct fails with a clash set without that point, the right disjunct is skipped, otherwise it is tried with the points the failure depended on. A rejection with clash set D is proved to rule out every model, in any universes, that satisfies the label of every node whose points lie in D (FullModel). Clashes are detected on insertion; definitions A ⊑ C are unfolded lazily. satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions, closes the table under the restrictions of transitive roles and runs the tableau from one blank named node per individual. An acceptance is proved to come with a model (in Type) of the role hierarchy in which the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at its named nodes, with named nodes related only along links when there are no role axioms and different named nodes as different elements; a rejection is proved to rule out every such model in any universes. A nominal or a cardinality restriction that reaches a label gives no answer, and otherwise None reports only a usize capacity limit.

requirements.requirement: Verified class parts with absorption: copy_iri_class
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual class parts of an axiom closure for the tableaux (shi_ontology::class_parts), proved against the Direct Semantics. Every class axiom over ALCIQ class expressions becomes inclusions: a subclass axiom one, equivalent classes the first member in every other member and back, disjoint classes every member in the complement of every later member, and a disjoint union the class in the union of its members and every member in the class, which the members also partition. An inclusion with an absorbable left side becomes a definition A ⊑ C unfolded lazily (a named class directly, ∃r.E ⊑ D as E ⊑ ∀r⁻.D, and E ⊓ F ⊓ … ⊑ D as E ⊑ ¬F ⊔ … ⊔ D); every other inclusion conjoins ¬C ⊔ D onto the TBox concept, a domain or range of an object property expression conjoins ∀r⁻.C or ∀r.C, and a functional or inverse functional object property conjoins ≤1 r.⊤ or ≤1 r⁻.⊤. Assertions, individual equalities and inequalities, and role axioms add no part. In every interpretation fixing owl:Thing and owl:Nothing the TBox concept holds everywhere and the definitions hold exactly when every class axiom holds; the parts are computed only for supported axioms, and always when every axiom is supported and the definitions fit in the usize range.

requirements.requirement: Verified SHI ontology queries on the completion graph tableau: proper_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual consistency, class satisfiability, subsumption and instance checking for SHOIQ axiom closures with assertions and individual equalities and inequalities (shi_ontology), decided by the verified completion graph tableau or by the verified completion forest, and proved exact for the OWL 2 Direct Semantics in any universes. Class axioms over ALCIQO expressions become the TBox concept and lazily unfolded definitions, functional and inverse functional object properties maximum restrictions in the TBox concept, the role axioms (inclusions without chains, equivalences, inverses, symmetry and transitivity of object property expressions) a closed role hierarchy, class assertions and query concepts facts at the nodes of their individuals, and object property assertions links; the members of every SameIndividual axiom share the node of their representative, and the individuals of the nominals of the closure get nodes too. A question whose concepts have no number restriction and no nominal, about a closure without negative assertions next to role axioms, goes to the completion graph tableau, whose models keep different nodes apart: there a negative object property assertion is refuted exactly by a link in either orientation between its individuals' nodes, and a DifferentIndividuals axiom exactly when two of its members share a node. Every other question goes to the completion forest, which merges individuals when a maximum restriction or a nominal requires it, with the nominal of every individual at its node, the members of every inequality outside the nominals of the later members, and the universal restriction to the complement of the target's nominal at the source of every negative assertion as further facts (Rowl.ShiNominals). An acceptance comes with an actual OWL model of the closure built from the tableau's model, with every individual at its node, which is where the forest's model places the individual of every nominal, and every OWL model forces acceptance. The queries answer only on supported axioms and Translatable expressions whose nominals are of named individuals, in a question only of individuals the closure has; no answer is given for built-in object properties in concepts, definitions, role axioms or assertions, for number restrictions on roles that are not simple, when a maximum restriction of the completion forest at the node of an individual counts an anonymous tree node that is no child of it, reached through a nominal, or when a usize limit is reached.

A question whose concepts have no number restriction and no nominal, about a closure without negative assertions next to role axioms, goes to the completion graph tableau, whose models keep different nodes apart: there a negative object property assertion is refuted exactly by a link in either orientation between its individuals' nodes, and a DifferentIndividuals axiom exactly when two of its members share a node. Every other question goes to the completion forest, which merges individuals when a maximum restriction or a nominal requires it, with the nominal of every individual at its node, the members of every inequality outside the nominals of the later members, and the universal restriction to the complement of the target's nominal at the source of every negative assertion as further facts (Rowl.ShiNominals). An acceptance comes with an actual OWL model of the closure built from the tableau's model, with every individual at its node, which is where the forest's model places the individual of every nominal, and every OWL model forces acceptance. The queries answer only on supported axioms and Translatable expressions whose nominals are of named individuals, in a question only of individuals the closure has; no answer is given for built-in object properties in concepts, definitions, role axioms or assertions, for number restrictions on roles that are not simple, when a maximum restriction of the completion forest at the node of an individual counts an anonymous tree node that is no child of it, reached through a nominal, or when a usize limit is reached.

A question whose concepts have no number restriction and no nominal, about a closure without negative assertions next to role axioms, goes to the completion graph tableau, whose models keep different nodes apart: there a negative object property assertion is refuted exactly by a link in either orientation between its individuals' nodes, and a DifferentIndividuals axiom exactly when two of its members share a node. Every other question goes to the completion forest, which merges individuals when a maximum restriction or a nominal requires it, with the nominal of every individual at its node, the members of every inequality outside the nominals of the later members, and the universal restriction to the complement of the target's nominal at the source of every negative assertion as further facts (Rowl.ShiNominals). An acceptance comes with an actual OWL model of the closure built from the tableau's model, with every individual at its node, which is where the forest's model places the individual of every nominal, and every OWL model forces acceptance. The queries answer only on supported axioms and Translatable expressions whose nominals are of named individuals, in a question only of individuals the closure has; no answer is given for built-in object properties in concepts, definitions, role axioms or assertions, for number restrictions on roles that are not simple, when a maximum restriction of the completion forest at the node of an individual counts an anonymous tree node that is no child of it, reached through a nominal, or when a usize limit is reached.

requirements.requirement: Verified rule search of the completion forest: representative_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual rule search of the completion forest for SHOIQ with named individuals (forest::next_step). The forest has one root per named individual and trees of anonymous nodes; a tree node's edge from its parent carries a list of roles, merges of named nodes are read through the individuals' representatives (same), and merges of tree nodes into named nodes add edges from their parents, named or tree nodes, to named nodes. The neighbours of a node along a role (forest::neighbours) are proved to be listed exactly and once each: its active children along an included role, its parent along an included inverse role, the named nodes that a link relates to it, and the nodes that an added edge from a live node (active and not blocked: Live, forest::live) relates to it. The named node of an individual (NominalRoot, forest::nominal_root) is the representative of the node of the first requirement with its nominal. The search is proved exact: it returns a concept that an active node lacks and that the requirements of the individuals merged into it, the TBox concept, an unfolding or its seed requires, or that a tree edge, a link or an added edge from a live node requires of either end (AddNeeds); else an active node with a nominal whose named node is another node (forest::nominal_node), with no answer when the individual of a nominal, or of the complement of one, in the label of an active node has no named node; else a neighbour that decides neither the filler of a maximum restriction nor its complement (the choose rule); else a maximum restriction with more neighbours satisfying its filler than it allows (Excess), with no answer when a maximum restriction of a named node counts a tree node that is no child of it, which the model may repeat (Repeated, Unrepeated, forest::repeated_satisfying); else an existential or minimum restriction of an unblocked active node that lacks neighbours satisfying its filler (Enough) and that it has not expanded; it reports Done exactly for a complete forest (Complete), where every such restriction of an unblocked active node has enough neighbours and every nominal of an active node is on the named node of its individual, whose complements have named nodes too (NominalOkAt), and Stuck otherwise. Blocking is pairwise: a tree node is blocked when some tree node on its path has the label, the parent's label and the roles from the parent of a tree node above it whose parent is a tree node (Blocked), proved decided by forest::blocked. The rules that apply the steps and the run are proved in Rowl.ForestOps, Rowl.ForestSteps and Rowl.Forest.

requirements.requirement: Verified operation of the completion forest: copy_roles_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual operations the rules of the completion forest apply (forest.rs), each proved exact: copying the forest reproduces it; adding an item to a label appends it and joins the branch points; the pending entries of a label list it; creating children appends that many tree nodes with one role, the seed and the given points; differences between new nodes cover exactly the pairs among them; the branch points a rule rests on cover the nodes near it (its parent, active children and the named nodes a link or added edge relates to it) and the added edges at it, and come from nodes and edges only; the differences among chosen nodes, the pairs of chosen nodes not known to differ, the first nodes of a list and the orientation of a pair are as specified; and the parts of a merge are exact: moving the roles of a merged child onto the parent edge or a sibling, adding edges from the parent of a merged tree node to a named node, carrying the added edges of a merged tree node over to the target (forest::carried, CarriedEdge), renaming an individual's representative, inheriting the differences of the merged node, and pruning, which deactivates every tree node below an inactive parent.

requirements.requirement: Verified structural step of the completion forest: expanded_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: The two structural steps of the completion forest (forest::expanded, forest::moved, forest::merged), proved exact and proved to keep the invariant, to decrease the measure and to carry models over. Expanding an existential or minimum restriction of an active unblocked node appends its children along its role with its filler as their seed and the node's branch points, pairwise different, and marks the restriction as expanded; the node loses more weight than all its new children carry, and a model where the restriction holds at the node has different witnesses for the children (created_models). A merge of one node into another (MergeShape), of two neighbours of a node oriented as forest::orient does (orient_shape) or of a node into the named node of its nominal, hands the edge of a merged tree node over to its grandparent, to a sibling or, as an added edge from its parent, to a named node, and carries its added edges over to the target (moved_carried), or passes the individuals of a merged named node on; inherits its differences; deactivates it with its subtree; and makes the target depend on the merge (Merged); the merged node no longer counts in the measure, and a model that places both nodes on one element models the merged forest with the label of the merged node at the target (merged_models).

A merge of one node into another (MergeShape), of two neighbours of a node oriented as forest::orient does (orient_shape) or of a node into the named node of its nominal, hands the edge of a merged tree node over to its grandparent, to a sibling or, as an added edge from its parent, to a named node, and carries its added edges over to the target (moved_carried), or passes the individuals of a merged named node on; inherits its differences; deactivates it with its subtree; and makes the target depend on the merge (Merged); the merged node no longer counts in the measure, and a model that places both nodes on one element models the merged forest with the label of the merged node at the target (merged_models).

requirements.requirement: Verified run of the completion forest: holds_literal
requirements.implementation_scope: Termination of the completion forest for SHOIQ and the meaning of its rejections (forest::run, forest::satisfiable). Every rule application adds a literal to the label of an active node, expands a restriction of an unblocked node, merges two neighbours, or merges a node into the named node of its nominal, and each decreases the measure, so run terminates on every forest that keeps the invariant (run_correct). An acceptance comes with a complete forest that keeps the invariant; a rejection with a set of branch points below the next free one rules out every model, in any universes, that holds under those points. Branching on a disjunction or on a neighbour's choice for a maximum restriction retries the second alternative only when the first failure depends on the new branch point (branch_correct); the merge rule tries the pairs of its first n + 1 counted neighbours that are not known to differ in turn, since in every model of the restriction two of them coincide (merge_rule_correct, choices_correct). Every model places a node with a nominal and the named node of its individual on the individual, so the merge of the nominal rule, at any depth, is forced and a difference between them is a clash (nominal_correct). forest::satisfiable interns the facts, the TBox concept and the definitions, closes the table under the transitive roles, declines number restrictions on roles that are not simple, starts from one root per individual and runs the forest; it is proved to terminate, its false answers rule out every model of the role hierarchy, the TBox concept, the definitions, the facts and the links, and its true answers come with a complete forest that keeps the invariant for the interned input (satisfiable_answers); it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction is on a non-simple role, a maximum restriction of a named node counts a tree node that is no child of it, or the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node. The model of a complete forest, and with it the exactness of true answers, is proved in Rowl.ForestModel.

requirements.requirement: Verified model of the completion forest: blocked_down

The model is the unravelling of the forest under pairwise blocking (independent of how the forest was built): its elements are the paths from an active named node through active children, where a blocked child stands for a node above it whose label, parent's label and roles it repeats; a named class holds where the label of a path's newest node lists it, an individual with a named node is the path of that node (nominalPlace), and an object property relates a path to its extensions along the roles of the child's edge, back to its prefix along their inverses, and paths whose newest nodes a link or an added edge from a live node relates, closed under the transitive roles it includes. Every neighbour of a node in the forest has a neighbour path with the same label, a live node having a path of its own (live_path), and every neighbour path comes from exactly one neighbour (step_of_neighbour, neighbour_of_step, corr_function); a neighbour has only one neighbour path unless it is a tree node that is no child of a named node, which the model repeats and which no maximum restriction of a named node in a complete forest counts (corr_unique, corr_third), so for a complete forest that keeps the invariant every path satisfies every entry its label satisfies, including minimum and maximum restrictions on simple roles and nominals and their complements, since a nominal is only on the named node of its individual, whose label also lists the nominal of its requirement (truth), and the model respects the role hierarchy and satisfies the TBox concept, the unfoldings, the requirements and the links (model_of_complete). satisfiable_correct: forest::satisfiable terminates; its true answers come with a model in Type of the role hierarchy where the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at the elements of its individuals, and its false answers rule out every such model in any universes; it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction counts along a role that is not simple, a maximum restriction of a named node counts a tree node that is no child of it, or the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node. The ontology queries use the forest for questions that count (Rowl.ShiOntology).

Every neighbour of a node in the forest has a neighbour path with the same label, a live node having a path of its own (live_path), and every neighbour path comes from exactly one neighbour (step_of_neighbour, neighbour_of_step, corr_function); a neighbour has only one neighbour path unless it is a tree node that is no child of a named node, which the model repeats and which no maximum restriction of a named node in a complete forest counts (corr_unique, corr_third), so for a complete forest that keeps the invariant every path satisfies every entry its label satisfies, including minimum and maximum restrictions on simple roles and nominals and their complements, since a nominal is only on the named node of its individual, whose label also lists the nominal of its requirement (truth), and the model respects the role hierarchy and satisfies the TBox concept, the unfoldings, the requirements and the links (model_of_complete). satisfiable_correct: forest::satisfiable terminates; its true answers come with a model in Type of the role hierarchy where the TBox concept and every definition hold everywhere and every fact and link holds at the elements of its individuals, and its false answers rule out every such model in any universes; it gives no answer when a structure would exceed the usize range, a number restriction counts along a role that is not simple, a maximum restriction of a named node counts a tree node that is no child of it, or the individual of a nominal or of the complement of one has no named node. The ontology queries use the forest for questions that count (Rowl.ShiOntology).

requirements.requirement: Individual kind total correct for exact individual source reading
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual Functional Syntax reading of individuals and individual lists is total and has exact result/error equivalence to an independent grammar. An individual is a full or abbreviated IRI resolved through the checked prefix table or a node ID with its exact label, both under the caller's IRI limit; a missing token reports the source length and any other token its start. An individual list is the maximal individual sequence before the closing parenthesis, which is left in place, with the caller's member-count bound checked before each further member, followed by the caller's minimum length, reported as an expected individual where the list stops. The reader is proved total by well-founded recursion on the token count; every result and first error has its derivation, every derivation is the actual result, an accepted individual consumes exactly its token and a list never consumes more than it is given. ObjectOneOf, ObjectHasValue, SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals and the class and object property assertions read their individuals here. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

An individual is a full or abbreviated IRI resolved through the checked prefix table or a node ID with its exact label, both under the caller's IRI limit; a missing token reports the source length and any other token its start. An individual list is the maximal individual sequence before the closing parenthesis, which is left in place, with the caller's member-count bound checked before each further member, followed by the caller's minimum length, reported as an expected individual where the list stops. The reader is proved total by well-founded recursion on the token count; every result and first error has its derivation, every derivation is the actual result, an accepted individual consumes exactly its token and a list never consumes more than it is given. ObjectOneOf, ObjectHasValue, SameIndividual, DifferentIndividuals and the class and object property assertions read their individuals here. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified individual equalities and inequalities for the ontology queries: intern_rest_correct
requirements.implementation_scope: Actual individual equalities and inequalities of the ontology queries (shi_ontology), proved exact. Every member of a SameIndividual or DifferentIndividuals axiom gets a node after the individuals of the assertions, with room for one more node. The members of each equality are united under one representative by relabelling: every node starts as its own representative, and uniting two nodes replaces the representative of the second by that of the first. Every representative is a node joined to its own node by a chain of equalities (the equivalence closure of the positions of members of one SameIndividual axiom), so every OWL model gives a node and its representative one element, and the members of every equality share their representative. The check for an inequality two of whose members share a representative, counting occurrences, is exact. No source/extraction assumption, admitted claim or custom semantic axiom is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Verified nominals of the SHOIQ ontology queries: not_mentions
requirements.implementation_scope: The nominals of the ontology queries (shi_ontology), proved exact. Mentions lists the individuals of the nominals of a concept; the checks for nominals (nominal, definitions_nominal, facts_nominal, closure_nominal) and that the individual of every nominal of a question's facts has a node (known, facts_known) are exact. The individuals of the nominals of the TBox concept, the definitions and the class assertions get nodes after the individuals of the assertions and equalities (nominal_individuals, definition_individuals, class_individuals, assertion_individuals). The completion forest also gets the nominal of every individual at its node (named_from), the members of every DifferentIndividuals axiom outside the nominals of the later members (apart_rest, apart_within, apart_members, unequal_from) and, for every negative object property assertion, the universal restriction of its property to the complement of its target's nominal at its source's node (refused_from): every such fact is proved to be one of these, and every individual, inequality and negative assertion is proved to have its facts. The ontology queries that use them are proved in Rowl.ShiOntology.
